title: cost-opt-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Ava Thompson
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit economics by shipping an automated defaults and autotune pipeline that selects batching/caching policies, quantization profiles, and conservative unit-econ recommendations for typical production workloads. This PR implements: 1) runtime heuristics and an autotune controller that suggests and applies default batching and KV-cache settings per model/route; 2) a quantization profile registry and auto-proposal flow for model variants (8-bit and mixed-precision) with safety checks; 3) a unit-economics tooling surface (UEcon) surfaced in the Console and CLI that shows estimated cost/token, expected latency trade-offs, and confidence bands. Scope: changes touch runtime scheduling, the optimize/autotune service, model registry metadata, Console UI telemetry hooks, and a small set of docs and tests. Checklist: - [x] design doc and Linear tickets linked (ENG-5473, ENG-5512) - [x] unit + integration tests for autotune controller - [x] canary rollout plan included - [x] monitoring/alerts updated for rollout (latency/cost regression alarms) - [x] docs and Console bits for UEcon surfaced in a feature flag Implementation notes: - Autotune controller (redwood/optimize/autotune.py) collects per-route seq-len distribution and tail latencies and computes an objective combining latency SLO violation risk and cost/unit. It exposes a proposal API that returns batching window (ms), max batch size, prefix caching TTL, and quant profile id. - Quantization registry (redwood/model_registry/quant_profiles.py) holds conservative, balanced, and aggressive profiles and compatibility metadata for fallback variants. Profile proposals annotated with estimated quality delta and fallback chain. - Runtime (redwood/runtime/scheduler.py) accepts prioritized proposals: when a model route is opted-in, scheduler applies batching defaults without restart using the existing dynamic config API; KV cache TTL changes are applied per-session with a migration path to avoid cold-cache spikes. - UEcon tooling (redwood/console/uecon/*) provides a read-only preview of proposed changes and an exportable CSV for cost analysis. Console changes are behind feature flag uecon.autotune.preview. Testing and rollout: - Local and unit tests added for proposal generation and quant profile compatibility. - Integration tests in perf-canary repo (referenced in the PR) for canary traffic shape. - Canary rollout pipeline: 1% traffic for 24h -> 10% for 48h -> full rollout; automated rollback on cost increase >5% or 95th latency regression >10%. Backwards compatibility: proposals are opt-in and require either explicit Console acceptance or an API toggle. Existing routes remain unchanged until accepted. Related: extends previous cost-opt autotune work and reuses telemetry hooks introduced in ENG-5120. Impact: expected median cost/token reduction 6-12% on read-heavy workloads and 18-30% on high-repetition prompt workloads depending on cacheability and sequence-length distribution. See release_notes below for details.

docs: update docs/cost-optimization and console guide for UEcon

merge_outcome: Merged after approvals from Liam Chen, Rajat Patel and Maya Rodriguez. Canary rollout pipeline triggered and monitored for 72h. No rollback required.
release_notes: Feature: Autotune proposals for batching, KV cache defaults, and quantization profiles. Tooling: UEcon preview in Console (behind feature flag) and CLI export. Impact: expected cost/token improvements on cacheable and repetitive workloads. Rollout: opt-in with controlled canary; automatic rollback if cost or latency regressions are detected.
notes_for_ops: Canary pipeline created in perf-canary referenced config perf-canary/configs/uecon-canary.yaml. Alerts updated in redwood/metrics/alerts.yml to watch for cost increases and latency regressions. Feature behind uecon.autotune.preview flag until full rollout.
manual_steps: 1) Toggle uecon.autotune.preview in redwood-console-config/feature_flags.yaml to enable preview. 2) Run scripts/migration/apply_kv_ttl_migration.py with dry-run then apply. 3) Monitor alerts: redwood/metrics/alerts.yml. 4) Accept proposals in Console or enable API toggle X-Redwood-Autotune.
impact_estimate: median_cost_reduction: 6-12%, high_repetition_reduction: 18-30%, risk: small 95th latency regressions during initial TTL changes if migration not applied carefully
changelog_entry: Autotune: defaults and UEcon preview added for batching, caching and quant profiles (feature-flagged).
notes: This PR consolidates work across multiple previous cost optimization PRs and centralizes proposal logic to simplify future rollout strategies. Contact: @ava for questions.
